_doc: MULTI-LANE re-test of WAL shard scaling. On the single-device c4d-standard-16-lssd (and the RAID0-striped -lssd ephemeral-storage layout) --wal-shards did NOT scale write throughput: every shard's fdatasync serialised behind ONE filesystem = ONE fsync barrier (a single-lane artifact, not a real ceiling). This suite instead runs on c4d-standard-64-lssd, whose 6 physically-attached Titanium NVMe devices are attached as RAW BLOCK and mkfs+mounted ONE device per WAL shard dir, so each shard's fdatasync hits an independent device queue (an independent fsync lane). It sweeps shards 1/2/4/6 (capped at the 6-device count — s7+ would spill onto the base volume and defeat the test) with the server pinned to 8 vCPU headroom (prior telemetry: wal is fsync-bound + CPU-idle) and worker-threads fixed at 8. Each config emits SRV_STATS (cpu_cores/inflight/durwait) + WAL_CKPT so fsync-lane saturation is visible directly. If throughput now rises ~linearly s1->s6, the earlier flatness was the single-lane disk, not the WAL design. REQUIRES these env vars when running (they are NOT encoded in this JSON): MULTILANE=1 (apply gke/durable-streams-multilane.yaml = one device per shard dir), SERVER_LOCAL_SSD_BLOCK=1 (create the server pool with raw-block --local-nvme-ssd-block instead of RAID0 ephemeral-storage), SPOT_SERVER=1 (cheap; a preemption just re-runs the affected cells). See MULTILANE_SETUP.md for the provisioning command + the VERIFY-AT-PROVISION-TIME checklist.
